scope.excluded: About text link, menu toggle, viewer action, YouTube link and unrelated page controls; disabled does not apply because all targets are anchors.

findings.observation: The same .header-cta is used on all three routes. At 1366 px it renders 176×42 px; at 390 px it renders 38×38 px and its text spans are hidden, leaving the WhatsApp icon. The element retains aria-label 'Fale conosco pelo WhatsApp'. Light and dark background are #8b6a40.

Home hero uses .button.button-dark; About and How-it-works CTAs use .button.button-copper. Both share base sizing, typography, radius 3 px and keyboard focus treatment; backgrounds and dark-theme colors vary by class.

findings.classification: contextual interaction variant / owner decision pending
findings.observation: On the Home hero, hover changes the button background but computed transform remains identity, although .button:hover specifies translateY(-2px). DevTools shows the finished .hero-copy > * public-reveal animation with fill both still owning transform. The same .button hover on About moves -2 px. The current behavior is context-dependent.

The Home story CTA is a plain text link with transparent background, normal-size text, weight 750 and no underline. Its hover state leaves the text color unchanged; focus-visible displays the theme-colored outline.

The authored public outline is 3 px with 3 px offset; light/dark theme overrides set #6e512e/#d8bc7c. In this Chromium session the computed values read 2.66667 px after stabilization; this report preserves the measured value and source declarations.

pendingDecisions.question: Should the Home hero button's hover lift compose with the finished reveal animation, or is its color-only hover behavior the intended result?
Should the plain story text link remain visually distinct from the filled buttons, given its separate size, treatment and hover behavior?

limitations: Static local state only; not a production or Deploy Preview capture.
No authenticated/private route, screen-reader, Tab-order, physical device, Safari/iPad or cross-platform validation.
The theme CSS states were selected by setting html[data-theme] in the browser; the theme switch control was not exercised.
Focus styling was forced with FocusOptions and match-checked; this validates the :focus-visible CSS state, not keyboard traversal.
All targets are links, so a disabled state was not applicable.
